transcript.text: This is a very proud day for USCIS and I'm thrilled at the role we played in bringing Operation Bargain Brides to a successful conclusion. I want to first thank President Trump and Secretary Nome for their leadership and commitment to restoring integrity in our nation's immigration system. I also want to thank our colleagues with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, the U.S. Attorney's Office, and the Document and Benefit Fraud Task Force for their outstanding collaboration in this effort. But most of all, I want to highlight the work of our dedicated officers here in our Baltimore Field Office, who helped bring this conspiracy to light. When our officers detected suspicious patterns in interviews, we worked closely with ICE, coordinating interviews, and investigations to ensure that we uncovered the full scope of this criminal enterprise and brought all those involved to justice. The results you see here today speak for themselves—the four ring leaders who collected millions of dollars for arranging fraudulent marriages have been arrested and faced serious criminal charges. We also prevented more than 120 aliens from illegally obtaining green cards, and we are not done yet. The arrests here and across several states yesterday are just the beginning. USCIS is continuing to work with ICE and the U.S. Attorney, and we will not stop until we have identified and prosecuted every person involved. The aliens who tried to defraud the American people yesterday left our office in handcuffs. The message is clear—do not engage in marriage fraud, or you will seek serious consequences. USCIS officers will remain vigilant, and we will work tirelessly to keep our country safe and protect our fellow Americans.

transcript.text: It was another busy week at DHS, so let's get into it. Secretary Nome joined fellow cabinet members for the first meeting of the anti-Christian bias task force. Thanks to President Trump's leadership and empowering law enforcement to do their jobs, ISIS captured more than 200 terrorists, including one of the most wanted fugitives in India, right here on U.S. soil. While the mainstream media publishes false narratives and pedal sympathy for criminal illegal aliens, DHS is debunking the fake news and protecting Americans. These criminal illegal aliens are not victims of the system, they are threats to our communities, and they will be removed. Secretary Nome stopped by the White House to speak with top podcasts, radio hosts, and members of the new media, spotlighting the department's work to keep Americans safe. And DHS made improvements to the systematic alien verification entitlement program, better known as the Save Database, to combat voter fraud, protect election integrity, and ensure taxpayer-funded benefits only go to American citizens. Under Secretary Nome and President Trump, the world is hearing our message. Being in America is a privilege, not a right. Break our laws, face the consequences, whether by air, land, sea or cyberspace, DHS is protecting the homeland and making America safe again. That's your wrap for this week. We'll see you next time as we recap the wins from the first 100 days of the Trump administration.
